label: paragraph_title
text: STAR FERRY

label: paragraph_title
text: ONE BOAT AT PRESENT

label: text
text: SPEEDIER SERVICE LATER

label: text
text: Early this morning only one Star Ferry boat was running, but the time taken for crossing was not far below that of ordinary times.

label: text
text: The "Star" Ferry operatives did not put in an appearance this morning and the restricted service is due to their assurance (after their first announcement that they were going to cease work) that they would be back as usual after all.

label: text
text: Bugjackets, deckhands and artifiers from the navy are manning the boats and the result of the observations and tests they have been making in the event of an emergency such as has arisen is to be seen in the good runs they are making and the ease with when they bring the boats to the wharves. It is hoped to supplement the service during the course of the day.

label: text
text: Later, I two boats are maintaining a service not far de然而 normal.

label: text
text: No Chinese are being allowed on the serry unless they are season ticket holders or have attended at the City man or knowhood kanway. The station and convinced those in charge of the tiger necessity of the business necessitating their crossing.

label: text
text: The raunai and Mongkok ferries are running as usual, but some launches have been directed.

label: paragraph_title
text: NOT RIOTERS

label: text
text: WORKERS UNDER POLICE

label: paragraph_title
text: SUPPLY EXCEEDS DEMANI PROTECTION

label: text
text: In spite of the fact that the "Empress of Asia" has had to call upon the services of schoolboys and masters in their endeavour to get it out of the harbour and on the Vancouver run to-day, it would appear that there are many qualified Chinese who are willing to act as stokers, etc., if they are guaranteed protection.

label: text
text: This is apparent from the response to an appeal made through the police for stokers for launches which have been affected. Many more applications were received than there were places and those who were engaged have given complete satisfaction.

label: text
text: Dock hands to replace those out on strike have been provided in abundance (also through the agency of the police) and the services of other skilled men and coolies can be obtained by firms in need who make application.

label: text
text: This morning a crowd of Chinese coolies and other workmen was to be seen outside the C. I. D. Office and these, it appears, were Chinese who had volunteered for service in any capacity provided protection was given.

label: text
text: The crowds observed under the superintendence of police guards yesterday and this morning gave rise to alarmed queries as to whether they might pot be mobs arrested in the course of demonstrations but they are merely workers under the protection they have asked for.

label: text
text: The trip to Vancouver on the s.s. "Empress of Asia" will be a memorable one from the point of view of the passengers and many of the crew.

label: paragraph_title
text: LINER'S CREW

label: text
text: The schools or colleges in the Colony having been closed in view of recent developments in China, many of the masters volunteered for service on the Empress boat. They have signed on in some cases for the most menial tasks. A Hongkong University professor is said to be among the galley boys.

label: text
text:
Schoolboys are discharging the less arduous tasks of stewards.
The Empress, it is hoped, will leave at noon to-day.

text: THE CHINA MAIL.

label: paragraph_title
text: London, June 26.

label: text
text: A report from Bombay states that Japanese exporters are buying heavy stocks of cotton on the strength of Press reports that Japan is preparing for war against China and is ready to sacrifice her Chinese markets by amassing enough cotton to tide over the period of hostilities. It is also significant that there is a great demand from the Far East for a certain type of manganese used in the manufacture of munitions.

label: text
text: Eleven Chinese have been deported as sixteen others arrested on the Belgian frontier. — Reuter

label: paragraph_title
text: HOME SPORT

label: text
text: London, June 26.— At Wimbledon, in dull but cool weather, the prospect of two appearances of Mlle. Suzanne Lenglen drew another huge crowd. The centre court was showing signs of wear.

label: text
text: In the fourth round Borotra beat Gilbert 6-1, 7-5, 6-3. Hennessey beat Gordon Lowe 9-7,8-6, 3-4. In the third round the Belgian champion, Washer, beat the South African, Sherwell 6-0, 6-3, 6-1. Thus a British trio went down before the foreign onslaught.

label: text
text: Hennessey was most superior at the net. He played with great opportunism though he had to fight for every game. Lowe was sure, accurate but seldom went to the net; he lobbed effectively and found the American's weakness overhead. Borotra danced his way through; he was at the top of his form and brilliant in his work at the net. Both are now in the last eight.

label: text
text: Jacoste accompanied Borotra into the last eight, defeating one of the two remaining Americans in Casey by 8-6,6-4,6-1 and he meets the winner of the Jacob v. Washer match.

label: text
text: Suzanne Lenglen earned the right to meet Mrs. Beamish in the last eight, defeating Miss Goldsack in twenty minutes by 6-1, 6-0.

label: text
text: Casey used a big gun service very effectively against Lacoste but was beaten by the machine like accuracy of the Frenchman in the rallies. Lacoste placed superbly and rarely had to run. He was not extended except in the first set. The programme was curtailed owing to rain at seven o'clock.— Reuter.

label: text
text: London, June 26.— At Prestwick in cool, cloudy weather there was a huge attendance. The leaders at the end of the third round in the British Open Golf Championship were MacDonald Smith 221, Compston and Jim Barnes each with 226, Abe Mitchell and Ray each with 228 and Tom Fernie 229.

label: text
text: After the complete 72 holes, Jim Barnes, an English born American, won with an aggregate of 300.

label: text
text: Kay and Compston were each 301, MacDonald Smith 304, Abe Mitchell 305. Five, including Taylor, followed each with 310, then came the amateur champion, Harris, with 311. Other prominent players were Kirkwood 314, Havers 316, and Dufkin and Tolley each 320. Reuter

label: text
text: "DAILY MAIL'S" DEMAND.

label: text
text: The Daily Mail in a lender pointing out the increasing serious illness of the situation in China as a result of Bolshevik efforts, complains that Soviet delegation is being permitted in London while the Moscow Government is spending large sums in inciting ignorant Chinese mobs to murder Britons.

label: text
text: The paper demands the clearing out of Bolsheviks from England.

label: paragraph_title
text: MR. A. J. DENNYS DEAD

label: text
text: Hongkong will learn with regret that Mr. Allen Junius Dennis died at Amoy on June 25 from influenza, followed, it is believed by an attack of pneumonia.

label: text
text: Mr. Dennis was with the Hong Kong and Shanghai Bank. He joined the bank in 1904 and came East two years later. He has served the Corporation in Shanghai, Tientsin, Malacca and Amoy. He was about 41 years of age.

label: paragraph_title
text: FRENCH SAVINGS.

label: text
text: Mr. Philip Snowden's Views.

label: text
text: “On July 1 next 3,200 million 6 per cent. bonds of the Credit National mature. These will become payable at the option of the holders. Another block of 8,236 million Treasury Bonds mature at the end of September, and a further ten milliards fall due the first week in December.

label: text
text: "If the situation in France is to be saved, and if resort to ruinous inflation is to be avoided, no time can be lost in dealing with the crisis. The Budget has not yet been voted, and credits are only available to the end of April. Enormous payments have to be made during the present year," writes Mr. Philip Snowden in the "World To-day."

label: text
text: A large amount of foreign debt will become due during this year, including 29,000,000 dollars due to America, and £11,727,000 to England. M. Herriot pointed out in his speech to the Senate that if, in the case of the internal debt which has to be renewed, two-thirds of the holders of short term bonds agree to renew their lendings the French Treasury will have to find the sum of 7,000,000,000 francs this year.

label: text
text: The renewal of these short term loans may well prove to be the final stage in the downward course of French finance, unless in the meantime something is done to restore public confidence. Already the flight of capital from France has become a serious matter. This has been confined hitherto, in the main, to be wealthier classes. The smaller holder is still the main holder of French Government stocks. If he becomes nervous then panic and chaos are unavoidable.

label: text
text: The French peasant has had an unfortunate experience with foreign investments. He has lost enormous sums by his Russian investments. It may be that he will rather take the risks of holdings in the bonds of his own Government than fly to investing in other lands.

label: text
text: "But all depends upon the confidence of the French peasant in Government bonds, and our hears that hoarding against the tax-gatherer and the risks of investment is increasing among the French peasantry. This is not to be wondered at when it is remembered that his capital investment in French Government bonds has depreciated by about two-thirds.

label: text
text: "There is a danger that under the new Government temporising tactics will be continued and no decisive action taken. In that case complete disaster cannot be avoided. In any case same measure of inflation is bound to happen."

label: text
text: "The financial crisis has probably postponed for a long time a settlement of the Inter-Allied Debt question. The French Government will make its financial position an excuse for a postponement. Great Britain is to continue to bear the burdens which the unwillingness of the French people to pay adequate taxation has imposed upon her."

label: paragraph_title
text: WOMEN'S DRESS.

label: text
text: The Jewish Telegraphic Agency has received from Warsaw the text of an important manifesto on the subject of women's dress which has been issued by the Polish Rubbinate to the Jewish population of Poland:

label: text
text: The Jewish people is disturbed. Every upright neurt is filled with pain, because of the latest ugly modes which have invaded our Jewish homes. Our daughters, who always that enguished themselves by their modestly and their moral behaviour, are allowing themselves to do missed by the dictatorship of "Nars" and bow down to it like slaves, wearing immoral dresses which have the purpose only of exciting lust. With regret, we see that this minister mode is spreading further every day and breaking up the barrier when has for thousands of years separated us from immoral peoples and retained in our people one best and the hottest and most pure. Woe to the generation which has lived to see this. Woe to the eyes which look upon it!

label: text
text: We, the rabbis of the whole of Poland assembled, as the responsable leaders of the Jewish people, appeal to you, Jewish daughters, women and girls, with tears of blood in our eyes. Recall the dark days of the Great War, recall the sufferings and the miseries through which the Jewish people have passed, the number of Jewish daughters who were outraged. To-day, when God has mercy has come to our ad, so that we can breathe freely, you, by our disgracultant stannons, are trying, good forbid to bring new troubles upon our people. How can you take this grave responsibility upon yourselves? What will you answer to God, blessed be His name? Every upright person with any ethical feeling regards with disgust and with revulsion your present-day clothing. The best of the Gentiles look upon you with scorn. To us Jews it is one of the greatest of sins, and according to the holy Jewish law—a married woman wearing this broadest dress may be divorced.

label: text
text: In order to do away with this disgraceful mode in Jewish houses we, the assembled Rabbis of Poland, have found it necessary to issue this appeal to all our brothers and sisters in the whole of Poland, that they should form special committees in all their towns, the object of which should be to consider how, with all the means at their command, to wash off this shame from our people and to restore Jewish spotlessness and pride.

label: text
text: We remind you that according to Jewish law every husband and father who tolerates this inmodesty in his home ought to be expelled from every Jewish institution. No Jewish man may enter a place in which there are women or girls wearing these disgraceful clothes. The tailors and dressmakers who make such dresses bear the responsibility of their sin.

label: text
text: We hope that our Jewish daughters who have shown such readiness to sacrifice themselves for the Jewish people will this time, too, how to our passionate appeal and will see the justice of our earnest exhortation.

label: text
text: EMERGENCY DISPOSAL OF NIGHT SOIL.

label: text
text: In the event of a strike of night-soil-coolies the following information as to disposal of nightsoll when water closets are not available is issued to the Public.

label: text
text: (1) In private gardens night-soil can be disposed of by burying at a depth of two feet. Care should be taken to avoid polluting a catchment area and to avoid the lines of rainstorm scours.

label: text
text: (2) Sewer manholes at convenient positions throughout the Colony will be opened from 5-30 to 7-30 a.m. each day for the reception of night soil. Such manholes have been marked with red paint. No manholes will be opened on the Peak.

label: text
text: (3) Nightsoil may be dumped over sea walls except in Causeway Bay and the Harbour of Refuge.

label: text
text: (4) In Happy Valley, owing to the absence of suitable manholes, nightsoil should be buried. With regard to areas available for the purpose enquiry should be made at the Eastern District Sanitary Office, Wanchai, Telephone No. Central 3218.

label: text
text: Any person wishing for further information should apply to the nearest Sanitary Department Office.
